previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain, gastroparesis, anxiety, depression, and PTSD was admitted for an acute flare of epigastric pain and vomiting. Labs showed mild lipase elevation, but ERCP and EUS revealed no acute pathology, biliary obstruction, or pancreatic abnormalities. Her hospital course was complicated by cellulitis at a peripheral IV site on the right hand, which resolved with IV and oral antibiotics. She also developed contact dermatitis from adhesive tape, managed with topical steroids. Abdominal pain gradually improved with an interdisciplinary care plan, oral pain medications, and dietary advancement. Diarrhea occurred during antibiotic use but resolved after completion of treatment. She was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating solids, with no pain requiring IV medication for over two days.
